What the numbers say

In this revision 67 option-selling candidates across 16 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 2 to 72 days out with a median of 16 days; 16 of the 67 expire within seven days and 6 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 68.7 for the AMD 432.5 put expiring 2026-11-06 (2 days): premium $1.51, strike 10.1% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 90.8%. Its displayed annualized yield of 63.7% multiplies a 2-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for AMD (88.0%), MRVL (86.7%), INTC (70.5%) and lowest for VOO (20.6%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 27 underlyings with a quote, 17 were up and 10 down when the report was generated; the median move was +1.77%. Rising share prices move existing short puts further out of the money and shrink the premium available on new ones.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-03), listed candidates went from 83 to 67 and the median time to expiry went from 10 to 16 days.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
